sources.title: OpenStreetMap drivable streets, barriers and traffic circles
sources.why: Streets outside Berkeley (Oakland, Emeryville, Albany, Kensington, El Cerrito, Richmond), joined to the County network at the city line; name, class, one-way, lanes and maxspeed tags. Widths outside Berkeley are assumptions (Berkeley medians). Barriers and traffic circles everywhere.

sources.title: Genasys Protect evacuation zones (WFS layer zonehavenv2:evacuation_zone)
sources.why: Zone outlines outside Berkeley (Oakland, Albany, Emeryville, Kensington and El Cerrito, Richmond, Contra Costa County). The City layer holds only slivers of these zones along the city line; its population estimates are kept where it has them.

sources.title: 2020 Census blocks (POP100) and Kensington CDP
sources.why: Population of Genasys zones that have no estimate in the City layer (counted from block interior points), the share of each zone inside the model area, and a check on the Genasys estimates.

sources.title: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, CA_AlamedaCounty_2021_B21 (lidar 2021, published 2022-08-10); USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, CA_NoCAL_Wildfires_B5b_2018 (lidar 2018, published 2020-03-18)
sources.why: Read overview level 2 (4 m) of each 1 m Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF via HTTP range requests; nearest overview pixel to each 4 m cell centre; Alameda 2021 has priority, NoCAL 2018 fills cells it does not cover. Overviews are averages computed by USGS/GDAL from the 1 m data. Bare-earth terrain. It does not show buildings, stairs, retaining walls, or whether a route is passable, and it does not determine fire behaviour.
